result.summary: The pedestrian environment features a sidewalk and a marked but faded crosswalk across a two-lane road in an industrial area. There is a lack of traffic control devices or signage to alert drivers to the crossing, and the sidewalk is separated from the road by a narrow unpaved strip.

hazards.name: Faded Crosswalk Markings
hazards.description: The zebra-style crosswalk markings are significantly worn, reducing their visibility to approaching motorists.

hazards.name: Lack of Pedestrian Signage
hazards.description: There are no signs indicating a pedestrian crossing, which may lead to drivers not expecting pedestrians at this location.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalk Markings
interventions.description: Repaint the crosswalk with high-visibility 'continental' style markings to improve driver awareness and compliance.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Crossing Signage
interventions.description: Install W11-2 pedestrian crossing warning signs to alert drivers to the presence of the crosswalk.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install curb extensions (bulb-outs) to shorten the crossing distance and improve sightlines between pedestrians and drivers.

result.summary: The environment features a signalized intersection with marked crosswalks and sidewalks, but pedestrian mobility is hindered by utility poles placed directly in the walkway. The wide corner radius and lack of physical separation beyond the curb suggest a design prioritized for vehicle throughput over pedestrian comfort.

hazards.name: Sidewalk Obstruction
hazards.description: Large utility poles and a signpost are located directly in the center of the sidewalk path at the corner, creating a significant barrier for people with disabilities or strollers.
hazards.location_in_image: Center foreground at the corner of the sidewalk

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction
hazards.description: The cluster of utility poles and mature trees at the corner may block sightlines between drivers and pedestrians waiting to cross.
hazards.location_in_image: Corner of the sidewalk where pedestrians would wait

interventions.title: Curb Extensions (Bulb-outs)
interventions.description: Install curb extensions to shorten the crossing distance, improve pedestrian visibility, and slow down turning vehicles.

interventions.title: Utility Pole Relocation
interventions.description: Relocate utility poles to the edge of the sidewalk or a furniture zone to provide a clear, unobstructed path for all users.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Upgrade the standard transverse crosswalk markings to high-visibility continental markings to increase driver awareness.

result.summary: The intersection is characterized by a very wide roadway with multiple travel lanes and a lack of clear pedestrian infrastructure. Crosswalk markings are either missing or severely faded, and there are no visible refuge islands, leading to high exposure for anyone crossing.

hazards.name: Excessive Crossing Distance
hazards.description: The wide intersection requires pedestrians to be exposed to traffic for a long duration without a refuge.

hazards.name: Faded or Missing Crosswalk Markings
hazards.description: Crosswalks are nearly invisible or absent, failing to clearly delineate pedestrian space to drivers.
hazards.location_in_image: Across all legs of the intersection

hazards.name: Poor Pavement Condition
hazards.description: Cracked and uneven asphalt in the roadway can cause tripping or difficulty for those with mobility aids.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Install continental or ladder-style crosswalk markings to improve visibility for drivers.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Refuge Islands
interventions.description: Install raised islands in the center of the wide roadway to allow pedestrians to cross in stages.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Construct bulb-outs at corners to reduce crossing distance and improve sight lines between drivers and pedestrians.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment is characterized by a wide, multi-lane intersection that lacks basic safety infrastructure such as marked crosswalks and pedestrian signals. While sidewalks are present, the large crossing distances and poor pavement quality create a hostile environment for people walking.

hazards.name: Unmarked Crossing
hazards.description: There are no painted crosswalks at this signalized intersection, leaving pedestrians without a designated or protected path.

hazards.name: Long Crossing Distance
hazards.description: The wide roadway requires pedestrians to be exposed to traffic for a significant duration without a refuge.

hazards.name: Degraded Pavement
hazards.description: Cracked and uneven asphalt in the intersection can cause tripping or affect vehicle braking performance.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Install continental or ladder style crosswalk markings to clearly define pedestrian space and improve driver awareness.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Countdown Signals
interventions.description: Install dedicated pedestrian signal heads with countdown timers to provide clear information on crossing time.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Construct bulb-outs to shorten the crossing distance and improve visibility between drivers and pedestrians at the corners.
